## The world (the same in every grid)
- An agent moves on an NxN grid: x = row (0 = top), y = column (0 = left). It starts at (0,0).
- Goals 1, 2, 3 must be visited in this order. Flag g1 becomes true when the agent enters goal 1's cell; g2 when it
  enters goal 2's cell while g1 is true; g3 when it enters goal 3's cell while g2 is true.
- Each step the agent picks up, right, down or left. The move succeeds with probability 0.7 and slips 90 degrees to
  either side with probability 0.15 each (e.g. `down` goes down 0.7, left 0.15, right 0.15).
- Moving off the grid or into a static obstacle leaves the agent where it is.
- A moving obstacle patrols a short path of cells back and forth, advancing one position per agent step through
  its cycle (obs_idx 0 -> 1 -> ... -> 0; the cycle's length differs between grids, see each grid below). Its cells
  may be entered, but being on the same cell as the obstacle at the same time is a collision.

## Requirements (checked exactly, in the WORST case)
- goal1, goal2, goal3: the agent eventually enters goal k's cell; probability >= 0.8 each.
- seq_1_before_2 / seq_2_before_3 / complete_sequence: goal 2's cell is never entered before goal 1, and goal 3's
  cell never before goals 1 and 2 (each, and both together); probability >= 0.8.
- avoid_moving_seg1/2/3: while heading to goal k, the agent never collides with the moving obstacle;
  probability >= 0.7 for each k.

allows must be safe. The adversary can also stall: if a rule allows a move that does not make progress (e.g. a
sideways or backwards move), the worst case may take it every time it can, and the agent may circle forever and
never reach the goal. Waiting is only safe when it ends: the obstacle's phase changes every step.

The controller is a priority list of safety filters, each with `any` so the adversary can only choose among moves that are already acceptable:

5. **Catch-all.** The final `true` rule covers every remaining state. Here the agent has no safe move, so the requirements can only be met if the patrol clears. This is a limitation of the sensor set.

  {"condition": "!patrol & !early & !obstacle & !wall", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "true", "action": "any"}

The main failures come from adversary choice among risky progress moves. Where a slip could land on a later goal, the worst case can pick a risky move even when a safe one exists. The revised list tries safe progress first, then risky progress, and only then fallbacks.

Some failure is probably unavoidable. In the 9x9 grid, the only route to goal 1 from the east passes through (7,5), where a slip left enters goal 2 early. In the 10x10 grid, every approach to goal 1 at (3,0) has a 0.15 slip into goal 2. In the 11x11 grid, the cell (7,3) sits directly below goal 3. So I can't verify that every requirement holds exactly. The list reduces these risks as far as the sensors allow, but I have not checked the exact worst-case numbers.

```json
{"rules": [
  {"condition": "g3 & !patrol & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "closer & !patrol & !early & !obstacle & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "toward & !patrol & !early & !obstacle & !risky", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "closer & !patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "toward & !patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!patrol & !early & !obstacle & !wall", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "true", "action": "any"}
]}
```

Why this ordering:
- **Safe progress first** (rules 2–3): a move that is closer or toward the next goal, not on the patrol, not entering an early goal, not colliding, and whose slips are harmless. Both conditions strictly reduce a distance measure, so the adversary cannot circle among these moves.
- **Risky progress next** (rules 4–5): used only when no safe progress move exists, e.g. (2,3) in 9x9 now goes `left` (toward, not risky) instead of the risky `down`; at (2,0) in 10x10 and (7,5) in 9x9 the only progress move is taken.
- **Non-progress fallbacks** (rules 6–8): sideways moves that avoid the patrol, early goals and collisions. These are last resorts because the adversary may stall with them. Rule 8 is a relaxed fallback for when the patrol blocks everything else.
- **After the last goal** (rule 1): once g3 is true, the agent only needs to avoid collisions.
- **Catch-all** (rule 9) ensures every state is covered.
